incident-bot: [P1] High error rate detected for Hemlock Health (hemlock-prod) - dedicated/vpc pool 'hemlock-dedicated-eu' - tool/function-calling failures affecting paging; initial spike 11:06 UTC. Auto-page suppression triggered.

mia (oncall): seeing 5xx parser errors in logs, looks like pagination frames are getting truncated by the toolcall parser. Customers reporting incomplete records. Paging rate jumped ~28% in last 3m.

sam (eng-runtime): can you paste the sample error? I want the parse stack.

mia (oncall): copied snippet from hemlock-prod-host-2: 
```
ERROR parsing toolcall response: unexpected EOF while reading JSON sequence frame
context: {"request_id":"req_6c2a","page_token":"eyJwIjo...","model":"rwd-open-13b-quant"}
stack: parser::seq::read_frame -> parser::json::parse_value -> io::read_exact failed
```

aj (eng-ml): that EOF + seq frame failure smells like upstream model/output changed delimiter style. Hemlock's toolchain expects JSON-lines with a trailing newline; runtime now emitting JSON-seq frames without newline between pages. Could be a model variant that dropped the separator.

rehan (cs): customer impact: Hemlock ops reported invoices missing last page and a few payment records skipped. They flagged this as high priority. Are we safe to route them to fallback?

lina (eng-sre): impact estimate from metrics: ~12% of hemlock requests in last hour had incomplete pages; downstream consumers retry logic not catching half-pages. If we can't fix quickly we should isolate tenant to avoid cross-tenant propagation.

sam (eng-runtime): mitigation options: 1) disable function-calling/tool-calls on hemlock dedicated pool (fast, degrades feature), 2) route requests to fallback model variant that preserves newline delimited outputs, 3) deploy parser-compat shim that tolerates JSON-seq without newline.

mia (oncall): which is fastest?

sam (eng-runtime): fastest is to flip tool-calls off for the tenant via policy. Command: 
```
# temporary disable tool-calling for tenant hemlock-prod
rdwctl policies update --tenant hemlock-prod --set tool_calling.enabled=false --env eu
```
Estimate 2-3m to propagate.

rehan (cs): Hemlock wants minimum downtime. If disabling loses functionality, they'll need to be informed. I can send a quick note and ask if they accept degraded behavior while we fix parser.

aj (eng-ml): routing to fallback model might be painless if we pick rwd-open-13b-compat which we've verified keeps newline delimited pages. But that requires updating routing config for the tenant: 
```
rdwctl routing set --tenant hemlock-prod --model rwd-open-13b-compat --pool hem-compat-eu
```
Propagation ~5-7m, but costs may differ.

lina (eng-sre): parser-compat shim: we can hotpatch a small middleware in the VPC ingress that postprocesses the stream and inserts separators when detecting JSON-seq frames. Risk: introduces latency and edge-case bugs. ETA ~30-45m for safe rollout with canary.

mia (oncall): I propose immediate plan: 1) Notify customer and prepare degraded mode message (rehan), 2) Flip routing to fallback model (sam) as short-term (5-7m), 3) Start building parser-compat shim (aj/lina) as medium-term fix, 4) If fallback fails, disable tool-calls entirely as last resort.

sam (eng-runtime): pushing routing change now. Executing: 
```
rdwctl routing set --tenant hemlock-prod --model rwd-open-13b-compat --pool hem-compat-eu --note "auto-mitigation for parser drift"
```
I'll watch rollout logs.

ops-bot: [deploy] routing-update job job_9843 started by sam (eng-runtime) - canary 5% -> 100% over 6min

mia (oncall): rehan, can you draft the customer message: what they should expect and the temporary limits? Also ask whether they can accept the fallback model (it has comparable quality but slightly different generation tone).

rehan (cs): drafting now. Sending: 
"Hemlock ops — we're seeing function-calling pagination failures for a subset of requests. We're routing your production traffic to a compatible model variant to restore full pages. This may slightly change response phrasing for a short window. If you prefer we can temporarily disable the tool-calling feature instead (will stop some automation). ETA for fix: ~1h. Please ack. — Red team"

Hemlock (external): acked. prefers routing to fallback variant.

lina (eng-sre): canary reports look clean at 5% — no parser errors in canary. Increasing to 50%.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] error rate reduced by 82% after routing change (11:14 UTC). Continued monitoring.

aj (eng-ml): starting parser-compat branch now. Plan: normalize JSON-seq frames by inserting newline between frames and tolerant deserialization. Will run unit+integration tests against hemlock sample corpus.

sam (eng-runtime): ops: adding temporary alert suppression for hemlock-specific parser errors to avoid noisy paging alerts. Remember to re-enable after mitigation validated.

ops-bot: alert-suppression applied for alert parser-eof-error.hemlock-prod for 1h by sam

mia (oncall): summary for postmortem: root cause likely model variant/compile changed serialization from NL-delimited JSON-lines to JSON-seq frames (no separator). Contributing factor: tenant-specific bridge-toolchain expected NL delim; parser was strict. Mitigations: routing fallback, parser shim RFC, add regression test in model onboarding to detect delimiter changes.

rehan (cs): Hemlock requested a post-incident review and a timeline. I'll collect impact metrics and customer-reported issues.

lina (eng-sre): follow-ups: ticket created RWD-INC-8372, assign eng-runtime + eng-ml for fix. Also recommend adding a tenant isolation playbook for serialization drift scenarios.

mia (oncall): ok closing loop: error rate remains low, customer acknowledged, parser-compat work in progress. I'll hand off to next oncall at 12:00 UTC.

sam (eng-runtime): leaving a note in the rollouts channel with commands used and the rollback step: 
```
# rollback: route back to original model
rdwctl routing set --tenant hemlock-prod --model rwd-open-13b-quant --pool hemlock-dedicated-eu --note "rollback if compat issues"
```

mia (oncall): thanks everyone. tagging next oncall @lina for handoff.

lina (eng-sre): taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate parser-compat canary. :mag:
